title: Nonempty intersections of injective ordinal maps
statement: In the simplex category, a map factors through a monomorphism whenever its vertex range is contained in that of the monomorphism. For two injective simplex maps e:[a] to [c] and f:[b] to [c] with a common vertex, there are an ordinal [p] and injective projections r:[p] to [a], s:[p] to [b], with re=sf, through which every compatible pair of simplex maps factors. The simplex category is the indexing category of simplicial objects [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 0164, the category of finite nonempty ordered sets; the range and nonempty intersection arguments are agent-written consequences of this definition

proof.text: For range containment, choose the unique preimage of each vertex under the injective map. The injective monotone map reflects order, so these preimages define a monotone factorization.

Form the finite subset of the first domain whose images lie in the second image. A common vertex makes the subset nonempty. Its increasing enumeration from Fin(cardinality) defines r. Factor re through f by range containment to obtain s. Monicity of re proves monicity of s.
A compatible pair has first vertex range in this finite subset, hence factors through r by the range lemma. Cancel f in the compatibility equations to identify the second projection.

theorem exists_face_pullback {a b c : SimplexCategory} (e : a ⟶ c) (f : b ⟶ c)
    [Mono e] [Mono f]
    (hne : ∃ x y, e.toOrderHom x = f.toOrderHom y) :
    ∃ (p : SimplexCategory) (r : p ⟶ a) (s : p ⟶ b),
      Mono r ∧ Mono s ∧ r ≫ e = s ≫ f ∧
        ∀ (d : SimplexCategory) (q : d ⟶ a) (t : d ⟶ b), q ≫ e = t ≫ f →
          ∃ z : d ⟶ p, z ≫ r = q ∧ z ≫ s = t
